The issue that I'm seeing is that Japanese developers are choosing not to localize some titles for the western market, referencing the sexualized content relative to western sensibilities. The community, comprised of a vocal minority, interprets this to mean that the Japanese have been scared away by vocal opponents of over-sexualization (or in some cases, even sexualization in general). What they aren't considering, however, is that Japanese business doesn't give a fuck about what western media says. They never have. Forgive me a tangent to clarify the point.

Japanese game developers have always been notoriously indifferent to not only western media, but even the vocal minority of western players. FFXIV (its original iteration) was a glowing example of this, and its failure wound up costing two senior executives at Square Enix their jobs. (Hiromichi Tanaka "stepped down" as head of the project and was given a quiet executive role in the company where he couldn't muck up any more games, and Yoichi Wada wound up resigning as CEO when SE couldn't recover the revenue they were expecting to have been generating from FFXIV subscription fees.) SE didn't clue in that their game was a disaster because of all of the criticism that came out of the beta testing. They didn't seem too worried about the pointed questions aimed at them by western media during their pre-launch press tour. What kicked them in the balls and forced them to take notice were the absolutely disastrous initial sales. What kicked them in the balls the second time was when they took stock of the damage such a disastrous release did to the Final Fantasy brand and the Square Enix banner as a whole. That was a massive turning point for Japanese developers. Japanese gamers at the time FFXIV was nearing launch commented often that Japanese developers basically develop what they want and tell the Japanese consumer that it's good. The Japanese consumer takes them at their word because that's part of Japanese culture. Japanese developers tried to develop a really awful game and sell it on the promise that it was good. Western gamers told them they were out of their daft minds. And for all the explicit expressions of this on forums, SE was only listening to the sounds of wallets opening, and those sounds were far fewer and farther between than they could point to as evidence of success.

Japanese game developers could care less when Jim Sterling has to say about what DOAX3 represents to western culture. They don't need Jim Sterling's narrative to figure out for themselves that portraying women in games as over-sexualized eye candy for all ages would damage their brands in the western market. They stand to lose more in future sales than they stand to gain from shipping softcore erotica games because the western market has steered away from the portrayal of women in such a one-dimensional fashion. That's not media. That's not SJMs. That's not feminists. That's consumers. The majority. The people who voice their opinions on forums and, more importantly, the much larger group of people who just buy their games and play them without a word. It's western culture that has sent a message to the Japanese that certain things don't sit well with us here, not the minority everyone is trying to blame. For every person on a forum thinking their voice has power, there's a dollar bill in someone's wallet that has far, far more influence.
